what_is_mvpf.heading: What is MVPF?
what_is_mvpf.description: The Marginal Value of Public Funds (MVPF) is a metric that measures the social welfare benefit of a policy per dollar of government spending. It represents how much value beneficiaries receive relative to what the policy costs.

applying_to_detention.heading: Applying MVPF to detention
applying_to_detention.paragraph1: Most MVPF work looks at policies where the person subject to the policy is also the main beneficiary, such as cash transfers. Detention is different. Jail is imposed on detainees but is justified as benefiting the general public. That is why this tool tracks both Detainee effects and broader Society effects when calculating the MVPF of detention.
applying_to_detention.paragraph2: Most studies on detention focus on marginal changes, like one extra day in jail or one additional person detained. This tool instead looks at the overall or infra-marginal picture for a facility, using Cook County Jail as the baseline case. It uses the full annual costs of operating the jail and the full set of impacts on people who are detained to summarize those tradeoffs in an MVPF-style framework.

detainee_values.title: Detainee Values
detainee_values.description: Detainee Values capture the total harm detention imposes on people who are jailed. We measure this using a willingness-to-pay lens, estimating how much a person would trade to avoid being detained. This reflects short-term harms, disruptions to work and family life, and long-term effects on health, income, and stability.

wtp_freedom.explanation: Represents the monetary value detainees place on avoiding incarceration. Derived from economic and wellbeing tradeoffs and interpreted as a willingness-to-pay measure.

harm_during.explanation: Captures immediate harms of detention, including loss of autonomy, exposure to stressful conditions, disrupted routines, and consequences for mental and physical health.

post_release.explanation: Reflects effects of detention that persist after release, including changes to employment, income, housing stability, and longer-run wellbeing.

society_values.title: Society Values
society_values.description: Society Values measure how detention affects public safety, victimization risk, and community wellbeing. These values summarize spillovers felt by people outside the jail and convert those effects into a common dollar scale for comparison.

crime_prevention.explanation: Measures whether detention reduces or shifts crime, and monetizes the resulting changes in safety and risk.

victimization.explanation: Represents monetized harm to potential victims or avoided victimization resulting from detention decisions.

community_spillovers.explanation: Captures broader economic and social ripple effects within households, neighborhoods, and local economies.

government_cost.title: Government Cost
government_cost.description: Government Cost reflects all public spending required to run the detention system. This includes daily operations, staffing, healthcare, facilities, court processing, and administrative overhead. It represents the fiscal cost taxpayers bear to support the current level of detention.

operational.explanation: Includes daily costs of running the jail: staffing, housing, food, medical care, and supplies.

court_admin.explanation: Covers court processing, hearings, paperwork, supervision, and other administrative overhead.

long_term_fiscal.explanation: Reflects downstream public spending or savings associated with post-release outcomes, service needs, or recidivism.
